From abb5f36771cc4c05899b34000829a787572a8817 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ben Morris <bmorris@anthropic.com>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 17:14:55 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] sctp: revalidate list cursor after sctp_sendmsg_to_asoc() in
 SCTP_SENDALL

The SCTP_SENDALL path in sctp_sendmsg() iterates ep->asocs with
list_for_each_entry_safe(), which caches the next entry in @tmp before
the loop body runs.  The body calls sctp_sendmsg_to_asoc(), which may
drop the socket lock inside sctp_wait_for_sndbuf().

While the lock is dropped, another thread can SCTP_SOCKOPT_PEELOFF the
association cached in @tmp, migrating it to a new endpoint via
sctp_sock_migrate() (list_del_init() + list_add_tail() to
newep->asocs), and optionally close the new socket which frees the
association via kfree_rcu().  The cached @tmp can also be freed by a
network ABORT for that association, processed in softirq while the
lock is dropped.

sctp_wait_for_sndbuf() revalidates @asoc (the current entry) on re-lock
via the "sk != asoc->base.sk" and "asoc->base.dead" checks, but nothing
revalidates @tmp.  After a successful return, the iterator advances to
the stale @tmp, yielding either a use-after-free (if the peeled socket
was closed) or a list-walk onto the new endpoint's list head (type
confusion of &newep->asocs as a struct sctp_association *).

Both are reachable from CapEff=0; the type-confusion path gives
controlled indirect call via the outqueue.sched->init_sid pointer.

Fix by re-deriving @tmp from @asoc after sctp_sendmsg_to_asoc()
returns.  @asoc is known to still be on ep->asocs at that point: the
only callers that list_del an association from ep->asocs are
sctp_association_free() (which sets asoc->base.dead) and
sctp_assoc_migrate() (which changes asoc->base.sk), and
sctp_wait_for_sndbuf() checks both under the lock before any
successful return; a tripped check propagates as err < 0 and the loop
bails before the re-derive.

The SCTP_ABORT path in sctp_sendmsg_check_sflags() returns 0 and the
loop hits 'continue' before sctp_sendmsg_to_asoc() is ever called, so
the @tmp cached by list_for_each_entry_safe() still covers the
lock-held free that ba59fb027307 ("sctp: walk the list of asoc
safely") was added for.

Fixes: 4910280503f3 ("sctp: add support for snd flag SCTP_SENDALL process in sendmsg")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Ben Morris <bmorris@anthropic.com>
Acked-by: Xin Long <lucien.xin@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260508001455.3137-1-joycathacker@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/sctp/socket.c b/net/sctp/socket.c
index 58d0d9747f0b..1d2568bb6bc2 100644
--- a/net/sctp/socket.c
+++ b/net/sctp/socket.c
@@ -1986,6 +1986,15 @@ static int sctp_sendmsg(struct sock *sk, struct msghdr *msg, size_t msg_len)
 				goto out_unlock;
 
 			iov_iter_revert(&msg->msg_iter, err);
+
+			/* sctp_sendmsg_to_asoc() may have released the socket
+			 * lock (sctp_wait_for_sndbuf), during which other
+			 * associations on ep->asocs could have been peeled
+			 * off or freed.  @asoc itself is revalidated by the
+			 * base.dead and base.sk checks in sctp_wait_for_sndbuf,
+			 * so re-derive the cached cursor from it.
+			 */
+			tmp = list_next_entry(asoc, asocs);
 		}
 
 		goto out_unlock;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File Modified: `net/sctp/socket.c`

#### Change:
In the `sctp_sendmsg` function, within the `SCTP_SENDALL` path (inside the `list_for_each_entry_safe` loop), a single line was added after the call to `sctp_sendmsg_to_asoc()` and the associated `iov_iter_revert`:

```c
tmp = list_next_entry(asoc, asocs);
```

This line re-derives the cached next-entry pointer (`tmp`) from the current association (`asoc`) after the socket lock may have been released and re-acquired during `sctp_sendmsg_to_asoc()`.

### Relationship Between Modifications

This is a localized, single-point fix. The relationship is causal:

1. The existing code used `list_for_each_entry_safe()` to iterate over the endpoint's association list, caching the next entry (`tmp`) before the loop body runs.
2. The loop body calls `sctp_sendmsg_to_asoc()`, which can drop the socket lock (via `sctp_wait_for_sndbuf()`) to wait for send buffer space.
3. While the lock is dropped, another thread or a network event can *peel off* the association pointed to by `tmp` (migrating it to a different endpoint) or even free it (if the new socket is closed). The stale `tmp` pointer then causes a use-after-free or type-confusion when the iterator advances.
4. The current association (`asoc`) is already validated upon lock re-acquisition (checks on `asoc->base.dead` and `asoc->base.sk`), so it remains a safe, live entry on the original list.
5. The fix re-derives `tmp` from the validated `asoc` using `list_next_entry()`, ensuring the iterator proceeds to the next valid association on the *same* endpoint list, regardless of what happened to the originally cached entry during the lock drop.

Thus, the modification directly addresses the race condition by refreshing the safe traversal cursor after the lock-drop window, leveraging the already-validated current element.
